title: An article's body, every kind of block

blocks.text:
Most pages on a small business site change a few times a year, yet the server builds each one from scratch on every visit. A page cache keeps the finished HTML and hands it straight back, so the *second* visitor never waits for the first one's work.

This piece measures what that saves on an ordinary content site, and where it stops helping.

Without a cache, every request boots the framework, opens a database connection, runs the queries for the page and renders the templates. With one, the request is answered from a file before **any** of that starts.

blocks.text: The fastest request is the one your application *never has to think about.*
blocks.attribution: A note from the build log

blocks.text: A cache hides a slow page; it doesn't make it fast. Pages behind a login, a basket or a search still run the full request, so they're worth measuring on their own.

blocks.text: How long we keep your details
We keep an enquiry for **two years** after we last hear from you, then delete it. Invoices are kept for six years, because the law says we must.
